title: Loan Margin on the Paid-Up Face of Universal Life Insurance Policies
content:
The protected face of an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy on overloan protection carries a loan margin, so that the paid-up face stays above a loan that keeps accruing interest after the exercise. The margin follows the loan balance standing in the activity history (the loan advances plus the interest capitalized less the principal repaid) as a share of the account value shown on the policy record, and multiplies the protected face before it is rounded to the cent.

## Margin table

| Loan balance in the activity history as a share of the account value | Loan margin |
|---|---|
| At or above **98%** (0.98, the high loan-margin ratio) | High loan margin, a multiplier of **1.02** |
| At or above **96%** (0.96, the standard loan-margin ratio) and below 98% | Standard loan margin, a multiplier of **1.01** |
| Below 96% | No margin |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, account value $300000.00)

| Loan balance in the activity history | Share | Margin |
|---|---|---|
| $294000.00 | 98% | 1.02 |
| $293999.00 | 97.9997% | 1.01 |
| $288000.00 | 96% | 1.01 |
| $287999.00 | 95.9997% | none |

## Reading the activity history (hypothetical)

Loan advances $260000.00, interest capitalized $31000.00 and principal repaid $2500.00 give $288500.00, which is 96.17% of an account value of $300000.00: the standard margin of 1.01 applies.
